metadata.title: A Short Proof of Bernoulli Disjointness via the Local Lemma

nodes.name: Standing assumptions: $\G$ infinite discrete, spaces Hausdorff
nodes.statement: Throughout, $\G$ denotes an infinite discrete \ep{but not necessarily countable} group. All topological spaces in this paper are assumed to be Hausdorff.

nodes.name: $\G$-flow
nodes.statement: A \emphd{$\G$-flow} is a nonempty compact space $X$ equipped with a continuous action $\G \acts X$.
nodes.origin_citation: standard (topological dynamics; unattributed in the paper)
differentia: equipped with a continuous action $\G \acts X$

nodes.name: subflow
nodes.statement: A \emphd{subflow} of a $\G$-flow $X$ is a nonempty closed $\G$-invariant subset $Y \subseteq X$.
nodes.origin_citation: standard (topological dynamics; unattributed in the paper)

nodes.name: minimal $\G$-flow
nodes.statement: A $\G$-flow $X$ is \emphd{minimal} if there is no subflow $Y \subseteq X$ with $Y \neq X$; equivalently, $X$ is minimal if the orbit of every point $x \in X$ is dense in $X$.
nodes.origin_citation: standard (topological dynamics; unattributed in the paper)
differentia: there is no subflow $Y \subseteq X$ with $Y \neq X$
the orbit of every point $x \in X$ is dense in $X$

nodes.name: Existence of minimal subflows
nodes.statement: A straightforward application of Zorn's lemma shows that every $\G$-flow has a minimal subflow.

nodes.name: Bernoulli shift
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a nonempty compact space. The space $X^\G$ of all functions $\G\to X$, equipped with the product topology, is also compact, and it becomes a $\G$-flow under the action $\G \acts X^\G$ given by \[ (\gamma \cdot x)(\delta) \,\defeq\, x(\delta\gamma) \qquad \text{for all $\gamma$, $\delta \in \G$ and $x \in X^\G$}. \] The $\G$-flows of the form $X^\G$ are called \emphd{Bernoulli shifts}, or simply \emphd{shifts}. A particularly important case is when $X$ is a finite set with the discrete topology; for concreteness, we may then assume that $X = k$ for some $k \in \N$. \ep{Here we identify each $k \in \N$ with the $k$-element set $\set{i \in \N \,:\, i < k}$.}
nodes.origin_citation: standard (symbolic dynamics; unattributed in the paper)
nodes.statement_short: The shift action $(\gamma \cdot x)(\delta) = x(\delta\gamma)$ on $X^\G$; the main case is $X = k$ a finite discrete set, identified with $\{0,\dots,k-1\}$.

nodes.name: joining
nodes.statement: Let $X$ and $Y$ be $\G$-flows. We view the product space $X \times Y$ as a $\G$-flow equipped with the diagonal action of $\G$. A \emphd{joining} of $X$ and $Y$ is a subflow $Z \subseteq X \times Y$ that projects onto $X$ and $Y$.

nodes.name: disjoint $\G$-flows
nodes.statement: The $\G$-flows $X$ and $Y$ are \emphd{disjoint}, in symbols $X \perp Y$, if they have only one joining, namely $X \times Y$ itself.
differentia: they have only one joining, namely $X \times Y$ itself

nodes.name: Disjointness forces minimality of one factor
nodes.statement: It is not hard to see that if $X \perp Y$, then at least one of $X$ and $Y$ is minimal.
conclusions: at least one of $X$ and $Y$ is minimal

nodes.name: Bernoulli disjointness theorem (Glasner–Tsankov–Weiss–Zucker)
nodes.statement: If $X$ is a minimal $\G$-flow, then $X \perp 2^\G$.
nodes.statement_short: Every minimal $\G$-flow is disjoint from the Bernoulli shift $2^\G$.
nodes.label: theo:disj

nodes.name: Furstenberg's earlier proof for $\G = \Z$
nodes.statement: For $\G = \Z$, Theorem~\ref{theo:disj} was proven earlier by Furstenberg \cite{Furstenberg}.

nodes.name: traps / trapped
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a $\G$-flow. We say that a set $U \subseteq X$ \emphd{traps} a point $x \in X$ \ep{or that $x$ is \emphd{trapped} in $U$} if the orbit of $x$ is contained in $U$.
differentia: the orbit of $x$ is contained in $U$

nodes.name: Theorem 1.2 (finite translates of an open set trap a point)
nodes.statement: Let $k \in \N^+$ and let $V \subseteq k^\G$ be a nonempty open set. Then there exists $n \in \N$ such that for all finite $F \subset \G$ of size at least $n$, the set $F \cdot V$ traps a point.
assumptions: $V \subseteq k^\G$ be a nonempty open set
conclusions: there exists $n \in \N$ such that for all finite $F \subset \G$ of size at least $n$, the set $F \cdot V$ traps a point
nodes.statement_short: For any nonempty open $V \subseteq k^\G$ there is $n$ such that every union of at least $n$ translates of $V$ contains a whole orbit.
nodes.label: theo:synd

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1.1 (derivation from Theorem 1.2)
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a minimal $\G$-flow and let $Z \subseteq X \times 2^\G$ be a joining. Our goal is to show that $Z = X \times 2^\G$. To this end, let $U \subseteq X$ and $V \subseteq 2^\G$ be nonempty open sets. We have to argue that $Z \cap (U \times V) \neq \0$. \begin{lemma} If $X$ is a minimal $\G$-flow and $U \subseteq X$ is a nonempty open set, then there exists an infinite subset $S \subseteq \G$ with $\bigcap \set{\sigma \cdot U \,:\, \sigma \in S} \neq \0$. \end{lemma} \begin{scproof} Since $X$ is minimal, the orbit of each point in $X$ intersects $U$, and thus $X = \G \cdot U$. The compactness of $X$ implies that there is a finite subset $T \subset \G$ such that $X = T \cdot U$. Say that a set $L \subseteq \G$ is \emphd{right $T$-separated} if $\lambda_1T \cap \lambda_2T = \0$ for every pair of distinct $\lambda_1$, $\lambda_2 \in L$. Since $T$ is finite while $\G$ is infinite, there is an infinite right $T$-separated subset $L \subseteq \G$. Consider any $x \in U$. For each $\lambda \in L$, we have $\lambda^{-1} \cdot x \in T \cdot U$, i.e., $x \in \lambda T \cdot U$. In other words, for each $\lambda \in L$, there is $\tau_\lambda \in T$ with $x \in \lambda \tau_\lambda \cdot U$. Since $L$ is right $T$-separated, the set $S \defeq \set{\lambda \tau_\lambda \,:\, \lambda \in L}$ is infinite, and we are done. \end{scproof} Let $S \subseteq \G$ be an infinite set as in Lemma~\ref{lemma:rec} applied to $U$, and let $n \in \N$ be the quantity given by Theorem~\ref{theo:synd} applied to $V$. Pick an arbitrary finite subset $F \subset S$ of size at least $n$ and let \[ U^\ast \,\defeq\, \bigcap \set{\sigma \cdot U \,:\, \sigma \in F}. \] By the choice of $n$, the set $F \cdot V$ traps a point, say $y$. Since $Z$ projects onto $2^\G$, there is some $x \in X$ with $(x,y) \in Z$. As $X$ is minimal and $U^\ast$ is nonempty open, there is $\gamma \in \G$ with $\gamma \cdot x \in U^\ast$. Since $y$ is trapped in $F \cdot V$, we have $\gamma \cdot y \in F \cdot V$, which means that $\sigma^{-1}\gamma \cdot y \in V$ for some $\sigma \in F$, and since $\gamma \cdot x \in U^\ast$, we also have $\sigma^{-1}\gamma \cdot x \in U$. Therefore, \[ (\sigma^{-1}\gamma \cdot x, \, \sigma^{-1}\gamma \cdot y) \,=\, \sigma^{-1}\gamma \cdot (x,y) \,\in\, Z \cap (U \times V), \] and the proof of Theorem~\ref{theo:disj} is complete.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to showing a joining $Z$ meets $U \times V$: take $S$ from Lemma 2.1 and $n$ from Theorem 1.2, pick a point $y$ trapped in $F \cdot V$ and a partner $x$ with $(x,y) \in Z$, then translate $(x,y)$ into $U \times V$ by minimality.

nodes.name: Lemma 2.1 (infinitely many translates of an open set intersect)
nodes.statement: If $X$ is a minimal $\G$-flow and $U \subseteq X$ is a nonempty open set, then there exists an infinite subset $S \subseteq \G$ with $\bigcap \set{\sigma \cdot U \,:\, \sigma \in S} \neq \0$.
assumptions: $U \subseteq X$ is a nonempty open set
conclusions: there exists an infinite subset $S \subseteq \G$ with $\bigcap \set{\sigma \cdot U \,:\, \sigma \in S} \neq \0$
nodes.statement_short: In a minimal flow, some infinite family of translates of any nonempty open set has a common point.
nodes.label: lemma:rec

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.1
nodes.statement: Since $X$ is minimal, the orbit of each point in $X$ intersects $U$, and thus $X = \G \cdot U$. The compactness of $X$ implies that there is a finite subset $T \subset \G$ such that $X = T \cdot U$. Say that a set $L \subseteq \G$ is \emphd{right $T$-separated} if $\lambda_1T \cap \lambda_2T = \0$ for every pair of distinct $\lambda_1$, $\lambda_2 \in L$. Since $T$ is finite while $\G$ is infinite, there is an infinite right $T$-separated subset $L \subseteq \G$. Consider any $x \in U$. For each $\lambda \in L$, we have $\lambda^{-1} \cdot x \in T \cdot U$, i.e., $x \in \lambda T \cdot U$. In other words, for each $\lambda \in L$, there is $\tau_\lambda \in T$ with $x \in \lambda \tau_\lambda \cdot U$. Since $L$ is right $T$-separated, the set $S \defeq \set{\lambda \tau_\lambda \,:\, \lambda \in L}$ is infinite, and we are done.
nodes.statement_short: By minimality and compactness $X = T \cdot U$ for finite $T$; an infinite right $T$-separated $L$ gives infinitely many distinct $\lambda\tau_\lambda$ with $x \in \lambda\tau_\lambda \cdot U$.

nodes.name: right $T$-separated set
nodes.statement: Say that a set $L \subseteq \G$ is \emphd{right $T$-separated} if $\lambda_1T \cap \lambda_2T = \0$ for every pair of distinct $\lambda_1$, $\lambda_2 \in L$.
differentia: $\lambda_1T \cap \lambda_2T = \0$ for every pair of distinct $\lambda_1$, $\lambda_2 \in L$

nodes.name: bad $k$-event
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be an arbitrary set and let $k \in \N^+$. A \emphd{bad \ep{$k$-}event} over $X$ is a nonempty set $B$ of partial functions $\phi \colon X \rightharpoonup k$ with finite domains such that for all $\phi$, $\phi' \in B$, $\dom(\phi) = \dom(\phi')$.
nodes.genus: nonempty set $B$ of partial functions $\phi \colon X \rightharpoonup k$ with finite domains
nodes.statement_short: A bad $k$-event over $X$ is a set of finite partial functions $X \rightharpoonup k$ sharing one common domain.

nodes.name: domain of a bad event
nodes.statement: If a bad event $B$ is nonempty, then its \emphd{domain} is the set $\dom(B) \coloneqq \dom(\phi)$ for any \ep{hence all} $\phi \in B$; the domain of the empty bad event is, by definition, the empty set.

nodes.name: probability of a bad $k$-event
nodes.statement: The \emphd{probability} of a bad $k$-event $B$ with domain $D$ is defined to be $\P[B] \coloneqq |B|/k^{|D|}$.

nodes.name: avoids
nodes.statement: A map $f \colon X \to k$ \emphd{avoids} a bad event $B$ if there is no $\phi \in B$ such that $\phi \subseteq f$.
differentia: there is no $\phi \in B$ such that $\phi \subseteq f$

nodes.name: $\P[B]$ as a genuine probability for finite $X$
nodes.statement: Notice that if $X$ is finite and $f \colon X \to k$ is drawn uniformly at random from $k^X$, then $\P[B]$ is precisely the probability that $f$ \emph{does not} avoid $B$.

nodes.name: $k$-instance of the LLL
nodes.statement: A~\emphd{\ep{$k$\=/}instance \ep{of the LLL}} over a set $X$ is an arbitrary set $\B$ of bad $k$-events over $X$.

nodes.name: solution to a $k$-instance
nodes.statement: A~\emphd{solution} to a $k$-instance~$\B$ is a function $f \colon X \to k$ that avoids every $B \in \B$.

nodes.name: neighborhood $\Nbhd_\B(B)$
nodes.statement: For an instance $\B$ and $B \in \B$, the \emphd{neighborhood} of $B$ in $\B$ is the set \[ \Nbhd_\B(B) \defeq \set{B' \in \B \setminus \set{B} \,:\, \dom(B') \cap \dom(B) \neq \0}. \]

nodes.name: degree $\deg_\B(B)$
nodes.statement: The \emphd{degree} of $B$ in $\B$ is defined to be $\deg_\B(B) \defeq |\Nbhd_\B(B)|$.

nodes.name: $p(\B)$ and $d(\B)$
nodes.statement: Let \[ p(\B) \defeq \sup_{B \in \B} \P[B] \qquad \text{and} \qquad d(\B) \defeq \sup_{B \in \B} \deg_\B(B). \]
nodes.statement_short: $p(\B)$ is the supremum of the bad-event probabilities and $d(\B)$ the supremum of the degrees.

nodes.name: correct for the LLL
nodes.statement: An instance $\B$ is \emphd{correct for the LLL}, or simply \emphd{correct}, if \[ e\cdot p(\B) \cdot (d(\B) + 1) < 1, \] where $e = 2.71\ldots${} denotes the base of the natural logarithm.

nodes.name: Lovász Local Lemma
nodes.statement: Let $k \in \N^+$ and let $\B$ be a $k$-instance of the LLL over a set $X$. If $\B$ is correct for the LLL, then $\B$ has a solution.
assumptions: $\B$ be a $k$-instance of the LLL over a set $X$
nodes.statement_short: A correct $k$-instance of the LLL (i.e. $e\, p(\B)(d(\B)+1) < 1$) has a solution.
nodes.label: theo:LLL

nodes.name: History of the LLL constant
nodes.statement: The LLL was introduced by Erd\H os and Lov\'asz \ep{with $4$ in place of $e$} in their seminal paper~\cite{EL}; the constant was subsequently improved by Lov\'asz (the sharpened version first appeared in~\cite{Spencer}).

nodes.name: Theorem 3.1 versus the full LLL
nodes.statement: We should mention that there are two respects in which Theorem~\ref{theo:LLL} in the above form is less general then the ``full'' LLL. First, Theorem~\ref{theo:LLL} only works with \emph{product} probability spaces such as $k^X$; this is a special case of the~LLL in the so-called \emph{variable framework} (the~name is due to Kolipaka and Szegedy~\cite{KolipakaSzegedy}). However, although this case is special, it does encompass most typical applications. For the statement of the~LLL for general probability spaces, see~\cite[Corollary~5.1.2]{AS}. Deducing Theorem~\ref{theo:LLL} from \cite[Corollary~5.1.2]{AS} is routine when $X$ is finite (see, e.g., \cite[41]{MR}); the case of infinite~$X$ then follows by compactness. Second, there is a more general form of the LLL \ep{often referred to as the \emph{General Lov\'asz Local Lemma}}, that applies to instances without a uniform upper bound on $\deg_\B(B)$; see \cite[Theorem 5.1.1]{AS}. However, this more general statement is somewhat technical and we will not need it here.
nodes.statement_short: Theorem 3.1 is the variable-framework LLL on product spaces $k^X$ with a uniform degree bound; the general-space and General LLL forms are not needed.

nodes.name: left $D$-separated set
nodes.statement: Let $D \subset \G$ be a finite set. We say that a set $L \subseteq \G$ is \emphd{left $D$-separated} if $D\lambda_1 \cap D\lambda_2 = \0$ for every pair of distinct $\lambda_1$, $\lambda_2 \in L$.
differentia: $D\lambda_1 \cap D\lambda_2 = \0$ for every pair of distinct $\lambda_1$, $\lambda_2 \in L$

nodes.name: Lemma 4.1 (large left $D$-separated subsets)
nodes.statement: If $D$, $F \subset \G$ are finite sets, then $F$ has a left $D$-separated subset $L \subseteq F$ with \[|L| \geq |F|/|D|^2.\]
conclusions: $F$ has a left $D$-separated subset $L \subseteq F$ with \[|L| \geq |F|/|D|^2.\]
nodes.statement_short: Any finite $F$ contains a left $D$-separated subset of size at least $|F|/|D|^2$.
nodes.label: lemma:indep

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.1
nodes.statement: First recall some basic facts about finite graphs. Let $G$ be a finite graph with vertex set $V$ and edge set $E$. A subset $I \subseteq V$ is \emphd{independent \ep{in $G$}} if no two vertices in $I$ are adjacent to each other. A straightforward greedy construction shows that if every vertex of $G$ has at most $d$ neighbors, then $V$ can be partitioned into $d+1$ independent sets. In particular, $G$ has an independent set of size at least $|V|/(d+1)$. Now let $G$ be the graph with vertex set $F$ in which distinct vertices $\sigma$, $\sigma' \in F$ are adjacent if and only if $D\sigma \cap D\sigma' \neq \0$, or, equivalently, $\sigma' \in D^{-1}D\sigma$. Every $\sigma \in F$ has at most $|D^{-1}D| - 1 \leq |D|^2 - 1$ neighbors in $G$ \ep{we are subtracting $1$ to account for the fact that $\sigma$ is not adjacent to itself}. Therefore, $G$ has an independent set $L$ of size at least $|F|/|D|^2$, and that is precisely what we need.
nodes.statement_short: Greedy independent set in the graph on $F$ joining $\sigma, \sigma'$ when $D\sigma \cap D\sigma' \neq \0$, which has max degree at most $|D|^2 - 1$.

nodes.name: independent set (in a graph)
nodes.statement: Let $G$ be a finite graph with vertex set $V$ and edge set $E$. A subset $I \subseteq V$ is \emphd{independent \ep{in $G$}} if no two vertices in $I$ are adjacent to each other.
differentia: no two vertices in $I$ are adjacent to each other

nodes.name: Greedy bound on independent sets
nodes.statement: A straightforward greedy construction shows that if every vertex of $G$ has at most $d$ neighbors, then $V$ can be partitioned into $d+1$ independent sets. In particular, $G$ has an independent set of size at least $|V|/(d+1)$.
assumptions: Let $G$ be a finite graph with vertex set $V$ and edge set $E$.
every vertex of $G$ has at most $d$ neighbors
conclusions: $V$ can be partitioned into $d+1$ independent sets
$G$ has an independent set of size at least $|V|/(d+1)$

nodes.name: cylinder set $V_\phi$
nodes.statement: For a partial map $\phi \colon \G \rightharpoonup k$ with finite domain, let $V_\phi \subseteq k^\G$ denote the clopen set given by \[ V_\phi \,\defeq\, \set{x \in k^\G \,:\, x \supset \phi}. \]

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1.2
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to cylinder sets $V_\phi$; via Lemma 4.1 pick a left $D$-separated $L \subseteq F^{-1}$ of size $\geq \ell_0$, build bad events $B_\gamma$ whose avoidance traps $x$ in $L \cdot V_\phi$, and verify LLL-correctness by bounding $d(\B)$ and $p(\B)$.

nodes.name: Equation (4.2): choice of $\ell_0$
nodes.statement: e \cdot (1 - k^{-|D|})^\ell \cdot |D|^2\ell^2 \,<\, 1 \qquad \text{for all } \ell \geq \ell_0.
nodes.statement_short: Threshold $\ell_0$ beyond which $e(1-k^{-|D|})^\ell |D|^2 \ell^2 < 1$.
nodes.label: eq:endgame

nodes.name: Minimality gives $X = \G \cdot U$
nodes.statement: Since $X$ is minimal, the orbit of each point in $X$ intersects $U$, and thus $X = \G \cdot U$.
nodes.statement_short: Apply minimality: every orbit meets $U$, so $X = \G \cdot U$.

nodes.name: Compactness gives a finite $T$ with $X = T \cdot U$
nodes.statement: The compactness of $X$ implies that there is a finite subset $T \subset \G$ such that $X = T \cdot U$.
nodes.statement_short: Apply compactness to extract a finite subcover $T \cdot U$.

nodes.name: Define right $T$-separated sets and pick an infinite one
nodes.statement: Say that a set $L \subseteq \G$ is \emphd{right $T$-separated} if $\lambda_1T \cap \lambda_2T = \0$ for every pair of distinct $\lambda_1$, $\lambda_2 \in L$. Since $T$ is finite while $\G$ is infinite, there is an infinite right $T$-separated subset $L \subseteq \G$.
nodes.statement_short: Introduce right $T$-separated sets and choose an infinite one $L$ (possible since $T$ finite, $\G$ infinite).

nodes.name: Each $\lambda \in L$ yields $\tau_\lambda \in T$ with $x \in \lambda\tau_\lambda \cdot U$
nodes.statement: Consider any $x \in U$. For each $\lambda \in L$, we have $\lambda^{-1} \cdot x \in T \cdot U$, i.e., $x \in \lambda T \cdot U$. In other words, for each $\lambda \in L$, there is $\tau_\lambda \in T$ with $x \in \lambda \tau_\lambda \cdot U$.
nodes.statement_short: Fix $x \in U$; translate $x$ by $\lambda^{-1}$ into $T \cdot U$ to get $\tau_\lambda$.

nodes.name: Conclude $S$ is infinite
nodes.statement: Since $L$ is right $T$-separated, the set $S \defeq \set{\lambda \tau_\lambda \,:\, \lambda \in L}$ is infinite, and we are done.
nodes.statement_short: Right $T$-separation makes the $\lambda\tau_\lambda$ distinct, so $S$ is infinite.

nodes.name: Reduction: show $Z \cap (U \times V) \neq \0$
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a minimal $\G$-flow and let $Z \subseteq X \times 2^\G$ be a joining. Our goal is to show that $Z = X \times 2^\G$. To this end, let $U \subseteq X$ and $V \subseteq 2^\G$ be nonempty open sets. We have to argue that $Z \cap (U \times V) \neq \0$.
nodes.statement_short: Fix a joining $Z$ and open $U, V$; it suffices to show $Z$ meets $U \times V$.

nodes.name: Lemma 2.1 (stated inside the derivation)
nodes.statement: If $X$ is a minimal $\G$-flow and $U \subseteq X$ is a nonempty open set, then there exists an infinite subset $S \subseteq \G$ with $\bigcap \set{\sigma \cdot U \,:\, \sigma \in S} \neq \0$.
nodes.statement_short: Quote Lemma 2.1: infinitely many translates of $U$ share a point.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.1 (nested proof)
nodes.statement: Since $X$ is minimal, the orbit of each point in $X$ intersects $U$, and thus $X = \G \cdot U$. The compactness of $X$ implies that there is a finite subset $T \subset \G$ such that $X = T \cdot U$. Say that a set $L \subseteq \G$ is \emphd{right $T$-separated} if $\lambda_1T \cap \lambda_2T = \0$ for every pair of distinct $\lambda_1$, $\lambda_2 \in L$. Since $T$ is finite while $\G$ is infinite, there is an infinite right $T$-separated subset $L \subseteq \G$. Consider any $x \in U$. For each $\lambda \in L$, we have $\lambda^{-1} \cdot x \in T \cdot U$, i.e., $x \in \lambda T \cdot U$. In other words, for each $\lambda \in L$, there is $\tau_\lambda \in T$ with $x \in \lambda \tau_\lambda \cdot U$. Since $L$ is right $T$-separated, the set $S \defeq \set{\lambda \tau_\lambda \,:\, \lambda \in L}$ is infinite, and we are done.
nodes.statement_short: Nested proof of Lemma 2.1 (minimality + compactness + right $T$-separated set).

nodes.name: Minimality gives $X = \G \cdot U$
nodes.statement: Since $X$ is minimal, the orbit of each point in $X$ intersects $U$, and thus $X = \G \cdot U$.
nodes.statement_short: Apply minimality: every orbit meets $U$, so $X = \G \cdot U$.

nodes.name: Compactness gives a finite $T$ with $X = T \cdot U$
nodes.statement: The compactness of $X$ implies that there is a finite subset $T \subset \G$ such that $X = T \cdot U$.
nodes.statement_short: Apply compactness to extract a finite subcover $T \cdot U$.

nodes.name: Define right $T$-separated sets and pick an infinite one
nodes.statement: Say that a set $L \subseteq \G$ is \emphd{right $T$-separated} if $\lambda_1T \cap \lambda_2T = \0$ for every pair of distinct $\lambda_1$, $\lambda_2 \in L$. Since $T$ is finite while $\G$ is infinite, there is an infinite right $T$-separated subset $L \subseteq \G$.
nodes.statement_short: Introduce right $T$-separated sets and choose an infinite one $L$ (possible since $T$ finite, $\G$ infinite).

nodes.name: Each $\lambda \in L$ yields $\tau_\lambda \in T$ with $x \in \lambda\tau_\lambda \cdot U$
nodes.statement: Consider any $x \in U$. For each $\lambda \in L$, we have $\lambda^{-1} \cdot x \in T \cdot U$, i.e., $x \in \lambda T \cdot U$. In other words, for each $\lambda \in L$, there is $\tau_\lambda \in T$ with $x \in \lambda \tau_\lambda \cdot U$.
nodes.statement_short: Fix $x \in U$; translate $x$ by $\lambda^{-1}$ into $T \cdot U$ to get $\tau_\lambda$.

nodes.name: Conclude $S$ is infinite
nodes.statement: Since $L$ is right $T$-separated, the set $S \defeq \set{\lambda \tau_\lambda \,:\, \lambda \in L}$ is infinite, and we are done.
nodes.statement_short: Right $T$-separation makes the $\lambda\tau_\lambda$ distinct, so $S$ is infinite.

nodes.name: Choose $S$ from Lemma 2.1 and $n$ from Theorem 1.2
nodes.statement: Let $S \subseteq \G$ be an infinite set as in Lemma~\ref{lemma:rec} applied to $U$, and let $n \in \N$ be the quantity given by Theorem~\ref{theo:synd} applied to $V$.
nodes.statement_short: Invoke Lemma 2.1 for $U$ and Theorem 1.2 for $V$.

nodes.name: Pick $F \subset S$ and define $U^\ast$
nodes.statement: Pick an arbitrary finite subset $F \subset S$ of size at least $n$ and let \[ U^\ast \,\defeq\, \bigcap \set{\sigma \cdot U \,:\, \sigma \in F}. \]
nodes.statement_short: Choose finite $F \subset S$ with $|F| \geq n$ and set $U^\ast = \bigcap_{\sigma \in F} \sigma \cdot U$.

nodes.name: $F \cdot V$ traps a point $y$
nodes.statement: By the choice of $n$, the set $F \cdot V$ traps a point, say $y$.
nodes.statement_short: Apply Theorem 1.2: $F \cdot V$ traps some $y$.

nodes.name: Find $x$ with $(x,y) \in Z$
nodes.statement: Since $Z$ projects onto $2^\G$, there is some $x \in X$ with $(x,y) \in Z$.
nodes.statement_short: Use that the joining projects onto $2^\G$ to get a partner $x$.

nodes.name: Translate $x$ into $U^\ast$
nodes.statement: As $X$ is minimal and $U^\ast$ is nonempty open, there is $\gamma \in \G$ with $\gamma \cdot x \in U^\ast$.
nodes.statement_short: Minimality gives $\gamma$ with $\gamma \cdot x \in U^\ast$.

nodes.name: Find $\sigma \in F$ sending $\gamma \cdot (x,y)$ into $U \times V$
nodes.statement: Since $y$ is trapped in $F \cdot V$, we have $\gamma \cdot y \in F \cdot V$, which means that $\sigma^{-1}\gamma \cdot y \in V$ for some $\sigma \in F$, and since $\gamma \cdot x \in U^\ast$, we also have $\sigma^{-1}\gamma \cdot x \in U$.
nodes.statement_short: Trapping gives $\sigma$ with $\sigma^{-1}\gamma \cdot y \in V$, and $U^\ast \subseteq \sigma \cdot U$ gives $\sigma^{-1}\gamma \cdot x \in U$.

nodes.name: Conclude $Z \cap (U \times V) \neq \0$
nodes.statement: Therefore, \[ (\sigma^{-1}\gamma \cdot x, \, \sigma^{-1}\gamma \cdot y) \,=\, \sigma^{-1}\gamma \cdot (x,y) \,\in\, Z \cap (U \times V), \] and the proof of Theorem~\ref{theo:disj} is complete.
nodes.statement_short: $\sigma^{-1}\gamma \cdot (x,y)$ lies in $Z \cap (U \times V)$ by $\G$-invariance of $Z$.

nodes.name: Recall independent sets and the greedy bound
nodes.statement: First recall some basic facts about finite graphs. Let $G$ be a finite graph with vertex set $V$ and edge set $E$. A subset $I \subseteq V$ is \emphd{independent \ep{in $G$}} if no two vertices in $I$ are adjacent to each other. A straightforward greedy construction shows that if every vertex of $G$ has at most $d$ neighbors, then $V$ can be partitioned into $d+1$ independent sets. In particular, $G$ has an independent set of size at least $|V|/(d+1)$.
nodes.statement_short: Recall: a max-degree-$d$ graph splits into $d+1$ independent sets, so has one of size $\geq |V|/(d+1)$.

nodes.name: Build the overlap graph on $F$ and bound its degree
nodes.statement: Now let $G$ be the graph with vertex set $F$ in which distinct vertices $\sigma$, $\sigma' \in F$ are adjacent if and only if $D\sigma \cap D\sigma' \neq \0$, or, equivalently, $\sigma' \in D^{-1}D\sigma$. Every $\sigma \in F$ has at most $|D^{-1}D| - 1 \leq |D|^2 - 1$ neighbors in $G$ \ep{we are subtracting $1$ to account for the fact that $\sigma$ is not adjacent to itself}.
nodes.statement_short: Join $\sigma \sim \sigma'$ when $D\sigma \cap D\sigma' \neq \0$; each vertex has at most $|D|^2 - 1$ neighbours.

nodes.name: Conclude via an independent set of size $\geq |F|/|D|^2$
nodes.statement: Therefore, $G$ has an independent set $L$ of size at least $|F|/|D|^2$, and that is precisely what we need.
nodes.statement_short: An independent set of size $\geq |F|/|D|^2$ is exactly a left $D$-separated subset.

nodes.name: Reduce to cylinder sets $V_\phi$
nodes.statement: For a partial map $\phi \colon \G \rightharpoonup k$ with finite domain, let $V_\phi \subseteq k^\G$ denote the clopen set given by \[ V_\phi \,\defeq\, \set{x \in k^\G \,:\, x \supset \phi}. \] Since the topology on $k^\G$ is generated by the sets of the form $V_\phi$, it is enough to prove Theorem~\ref{theo:synd} with $V = V_\phi$.
nodes.statement_short: Since cylinder sets $V_\phi$ generate the topology, it suffices to treat $V = V_\phi$.

nodes.name: Fix $D$, $\phi$, $\ell_0$ and set $n = \ell_0|D|^2$
nodes.statement: So, let $D \subset \G$ be a nonempty finite set and let $\phi \colon D \to k$. Let $\ell_0 \in \N$ be such that \begin{equation} e \cdot (1 - k^{-|D|})^\ell \cdot |D|^2\ell^2 \,<\, 1 \qquad \text{for all } \ell \geq \ell_0. \end{equation} \ep{Such $\ell_0$ exists since the left-hand side of \eqref{eq:endgame} approaches $0$ as $\ell$ goes to infinity.} We shall argue that $n \defeq \ell_0|D|^2$ is as desired.
nodes.statement_short: Fix $\phi \colon D \to k$, choose $\ell_0$ by (4.2), and claim $n = \ell_0 |D|^2$ works.

nodes.name: Extract a left $D$-separated $L$ via Lemma 4.1
nodes.statement: Take any finite set $F \subset \G$ of size at least $n$ and let $L \subseteq F$ be a set of size at least $|F|/|D|^2 \geq \ell_0$ such that $L^{-1}$ is left $D$-separated \ep{such $L$ exists due to Lemma~\ref{lemma:indep} applied with $F^{-1}$ in place of $F$}.
nodes.statement_short: Apply Lemma 4.1 to $F^{-1}$ to get $L \subseteq F$ with $|L| \geq \ell_0$ and $L^{-1}$ left $D$-separated.

nodes.name: Define the bad events $B_\gamma$
nodes.statement: Define a $k$-instance $\B$ over $\G$ as follows. For each $\gamma \in \G$, let $B_\gamma$ be the bad $k$-event with domain $D_\gamma \defeq D L^{-1}\gamma$ consisting of all maps $\psi \colon D_\gamma \to k$ such that: \[ \text{for each } \lambda \in L,\ \text{there is } \delta \in D\ \text{with } \psi(\delta\lambda^{-1}\gamma) \,\neq\, \phi(\delta). \]
nodes.statement_short: For each $\gamma$, $B_\gamma$ is the event that every $\lambda \in L$ fails to match $\phi$ on $D\lambda^{-1}\gamma$.

nodes.name: $D_\gamma$ is a disjoint union
nodes.statement: Notice that since $L^{-1}$ is left $D$-separated, $D_\gamma$ is equal to the \emph{disjoint} union of the sets $D \lambda^{-1}\gamma$, $\lambda \in L$.
nodes.statement_short: Left $D$-separation makes the pieces $D\lambda^{-1}\gamma$ of $D_\gamma$ disjoint.

nodes.name: Claim: solutions of $\B$ are trapped in $L \cdot V_\phi$
nodes.statement: Let $\B\defeq \set{B_\gamma \,:\, \gamma \in \G}$. We claim that if $x \colon \G\to k$ is a solution to $\B$, then $x$ is trapped in $L \cdot V_\phi$ \ep{and hence also in $F \cdot V_\phi$}.
nodes.statement_short: Set $\B = \{B_\gamma\}$ and claim every solution $x$ is trapped in $L \cdot V_\phi \subseteq F \cdot V_\phi$.

nodes.name: Avoiding $B_\gamma$ gives a matching $\lambda$
nodes.statement: Indeed, consider any $\gamma \in \G$. Since $x$ avoids $B_\gamma$, the following holds: \[ \text{there is } \lambda \in L\ \text{such that for all } \delta \in D, \ x(\delta \lambda^{-1}\gamma) \,=\, \phi(\delta). \]
nodes.statement_short: Avoiding $B_\gamma$ means some $\lambda \in L$ has $x = \phi$ on $D\lambda^{-1}\gamma$.

nodes.name: Hence $\gamma \cdot x \in L \cdot V_\phi$
nodes.statement: But this precisely means that for some $\lambda \in L$, $\lambda^{-1}\gamma \cdot x \supset \phi$, i.e., $\gamma \cdot x \in L \cdot V_\phi$.
nodes.statement_short: Translate: $\lambda^{-1}\gamma \cdot x \supset \phi$, so $\gamma \cdot x \in L \cdot V_\phi$.

nodes.name: Remains: $\B$ is correct for the LLL
nodes.statement: In view of Theorem~\ref{theo:LLL}, it only remains to show that $\B$ is correct for the LLL.
nodes.statement_short: By the LLL it remains to check $\B$ is correct.

nodes.name: Set up the bound on $d(\B)$
nodes.statement: First we bound $d(\B)$. Consider any $\gamma \in \G$. We need to find an upper bound on the size of the set \[ \set{\gamma' \in \G \setminus \set{\gamma} \,:\, D_\gamma \cap D_{\gamma'} \neq \0}. \]
nodes.statement_short: Fix $\gamma$; bound the number of $\gamma'$ with $D_{\gamma'} \cap D_\gamma \neq \0$.

nodes.name: Characterise overlapping domains
nodes.statement: To this end, notice that $D_\gamma \cap D_{\gamma'} \neq \0$ if and only if $\gamma' \in LD^{-1}DL^{-1}\gamma$.
nodes.statement_short: $D_\gamma \cap D_{\gamma'} \neq \0$ iff $\gamma' \in LD^{-1}DL^{-1}\gamma$.

nodes.name: Conclude $d(\B) \leq |D|^2|L|^2 - 1$
nodes.statement: Thus, \[ \left|\set{\gamma' \in \G \setminus \set{\gamma} \,:\, D_\gamma \cap D_{\gamma'} \neq \0}\right| \,=\, |LD^{-1}DL^{-1}| - 1 \,\leq\, |D|^2|L|^2 - 1, \] and hence we conclude that $d(\B) \leq |D|^2|L|^2 - 1$.

nodes.name: Set up the bound on $p(\B)$
nodes.statement: Next we bound $p(\B)$. Again, fix $\gamma \in \G$ and draw $f \colon D_\gamma \to k$ uniformly at random.
nodes.statement_short: Fix $\gamma$ and draw $f \colon D_\gamma \to k$ uniformly.

nodes.name: Compute $\P[B_\gamma]$ and bound $p(\B)$
nodes.statement: Then for each $\lambda \in L$, \[ \P[f(\delta \lambda^{-1} \gamma) \neq \phi(\delta) \text{ for some } \delta \in D] \,=\, 1 - k^{-|D|}, \] and since the sets $D \lambda^{-1}\gamma$, $\lambda \in L$ are disjoint, we conclude that \[ \P[B_\gamma] \,=\, (1 - k^{-|D|})^{|L|}. \] Therefore, $p(\B) \leq (1 - k^{-|D|})^{|L|}$.
nodes.statement_short: Independence over the disjoint pieces gives $\P[B_\gamma] = (1-k^{-|D|})^{|L|}$.

nodes.name: Verify correctness via (4.2)
nodes.statement: To put everything together, $\B$ is correct as long as \[ e \cdot (1 - k^{-|D|})^{|L|} \cdot |D|^2|L|^2 \,<\, 1. \] Since $|L| \geq \ell_0$, \eqref{eq:endgame} gives the desired result.
nodes.statement_short: Correctness reduces to $e(1-k^{-|D|})^{|L|}|D|^2|L|^2 < 1$, which (4.2) gives since $|L| \geq \ell_0$.
